extracted.intended_audience: brand marketers, PR professionals, communications managers and business owners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for brands and communicators to avoid public relations failures by checking data, crafting clear messaging, aligning actions with claims, and preparing crisis responses. Uses 2023 case examples (Emirates, Levi's, Lufthansa) to illustrate pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify internal data and policy alignment before public campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that any public-facing campaign or message is consistent with the company's actual policies and measured performance (e.g., pay gaps, diversity stats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites Emirates being exposed by the 'Gender Pay Gap Bot' which revealed a 34.2% pay gap — an instant PR fail because public information contradicted the campaign. Antipattern: publishing aspirational or celebratory messaging without auditing internal metrics and anticipating external fact-checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tokenistic or lazy diversity solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not present technology or shortcuts as substitutes for genuine representation; avoid framing AI as a sole fix for diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Levi's announcement to 'build customised AI models to “supplement and increase the number and diversity of our models”' was criticised as 'problematic and lazy' — critics argued it would be better to hire diverse models. Guidance: prioritise authentic hiring and representation, and be prepared to explain how technology fits into a broader inclusion strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent and specific about the role and limits of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: When using AI in campaigns or product imagery, clearly state its intended, limited role and how it complements human practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levi's later clarified AI was not the sole solution but an 'important part' — messaging should avoid implying AI fully replaces human processes. Antipatterns: vague or overclaiming statements about AI leading to public distrust and backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague or deceptive sustainability (greenwashing) claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustainability-related messaging must be precise and substantiated; vague 'green' language erodes trust and invites scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lufthansa 'Green Fare' and subsequent advert drew criticism and was banned by the Advertising Standards Agency. Guidance: make verifiable claims, provide evidence for offsets and environmental benefits, and avoid misleading impressions of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure advertising and claims comply with regulators and industry standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate regulatory review (e.g., advertising standards bodies) and craft claims to meet legal and industry rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lufthansa's advert was 'banned by the Advertising Standards Agency' — indicating that adverts and pricing claims can be subject to formal complaints and bans. Guidance: review claims for compliance before release and keep documentation to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear, specific messaging to build and maintain trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vague messaging and ambiguous topical language which can be read as deceptive or insincere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes 'vague messaging and deceptive use of topical language has led to a lack of trust.' Guidance: be precise about what you are offering, the impact, costs, and limitations; specificity reduces misinterpretation and backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate activist and social-media scrutiny around topical dates/campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: When running campaigns tied to social causes or observances (e.g., International Women’s Day), expect heightened scrutiny and prepare to address contradictions or criticisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Emirates’ International Women’s Day contribution was quickly amplified by the Gender Pay Gap Bot. Guidance: audit how proposed campaigns will appear under public scrutiny, and ensure actions match messaging to avoid being 'shown up on a global stage.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare crisis management plans and allocate resources for rapid response
rubrics_metrics.description: Have procedures, spokespeople, and resources ready to respond swiftly and effectively when messaging backfires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article asks how much time and resources are tied up in 'crisis management mode' after PR fails. Guidance: develop crisis playbooks, designate trained communicators, and rehearse likely scenarios to reduce damage and response time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with PR professionals and provide staff training to minimise PR risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage PR agencies or training solutions to manage media interactions and upskill teams so that communications align with strategic goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recommends 'working with a PR agency' and notes Digital Glue offers 'training solutions, including PR sessions.' Guidance: use external expertise for media relations, and run internal training so staff understand messaging, compliance and crisis protocols.
